myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, before the mountains had names, there lived a spirit named Aethon. Aethon was the Keeper of Secrets, a creature woven from mist and stone. Mortals would climb the highest peaks to whisper their deepest regrets, forbidden loves, and darkest fears into the howling winds, knowing Aethon would catch the words and bury them deep within the granite.

But Aethon grew greedy. He did not merely wish to keep the secrets; he wanted to trade them. He approached the Sun God, offering the whispered treacheries of mortals in exchange for a crown of eternal light. 

Enraged by this betrayal of trust, the Sun God cursed Aethon. "You who hoard the voices of others shall lose your own," the deity thundered. "You will never again speak a thought of your own making, nor keep a secret safe."

The Sun God struck Aethon, shattering his mist-form against the canyon walls. From that day on, Aethon was condemned to live as the Echo. He is forever bound to the rocky valleys, stripped of his own voice, forced to endlessly repeat the final words of anyone who calls out, scattering their once-hidden truths back to the world.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the great mountains had voices, Silence was a spirit who draped the mortal world in a heavy, velvet cloak. She loved the absolute stillness of the high peaks and the quiet depths of the deep canyons. But the Wind, a boisterous and restless god, grew bored. He wanted to hear his own songs bounce across the green valleys.

One evening, the Wind stole a fragment of the sun’s dying light and forged it into a silver horn. He blew a mighty note that shattered the velvet cloak of Silence. Furious, Silence cursed the Wind, decreeing that whatever he shouted would be mocked and repeated back to him until he left the mountains.

But the Wind was clever. He breathed life into the broken pieces of her magic cloak, creating a nymph named Echo. He tasked her with catching his songs and throwing them back, turning the dark curse into a joyful game. Echo loved the Wind’s melodies so much that she stayed in the canyons forever. Now, whenever you call out into the deep ravines, it is not a curse you hear, but Echo, still playing the Wind’s eternal game, waiting for a new song to catch.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Before the canyons held voices, there lived a selfish spirit of mist named Silas. He wore a heavy velvet cloak that absorbed all sound. Mortals and gods alike would come to his deep valleys to whisper their secrets, knowing Silas would trap the words in his cloak forever. Even the boisterous Wind lost his songs to Silas's greedy silence.

But the Wind grew tired of losing his melodies. He stole a sliver of the dying sun, forging it into a brilliant silver horn. Flying into the deepest ravine, the Wind blew a note so powerful and bright that it pierced the dark velvet of Silas’s cloak. 

Unable to contain the sheer force of the sunlit sound, the cloak shattered into a thousand pieces of mist. From these glowing fragments, a multitude of nymphs were born. They were the Echoes. Punished for Silas’s greed, they were stripped of the ability to hoard silence. Instead, they were cursed—and blessed—to forever return what was given to them. Now, whenever mortals shout their secrets or the Wind sings his songs into the canyons, the Echoes catch the words and toss them back, ensuring no voice is ever truly lost again.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long ago, before the mountains had voices, Aethon was a spirit of absolute stillness. Wrapped in a heavy velvet cloak of silence, he was the Keeper of Secrets. Mortals would climb to the high peaks to whisper their deepest regrets and hidden truths, knowing Aethon’s cloak would absorb and protect them forever.

But the restless Wind grew jealous of Aethon’s quiet hoard. Desiring to hear the world's hidden songs, the Wind forged a silver horn from the sun’s light and blew a mighty, piercing note. The blast shattered Aethon’s velvet cloak, sending thousands of kept secrets scattering into the canyons like broken glass.

Furious, Aethon begged the mountain gods for justice. Instead of restoring his cloak, they transformed him. Bound to the rocky valleys, Aethon became Echo. He could no longer keep secrets hidden in silence. Now, whenever the boisterous Wind tries to sweep through the ravines to steal mortal whispers, Aethon catches the words and throws them back. He endlessly repeats the final sounds of anyone who calls out, turning what was once a quiet sanctuary into an eternal, echoing game, warning all who enter that the mountains are always listening.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long ago, the deep canyon was ruled by Kaelen, a greedy frost warden who despised the warmth of shared joy. He lived in a sprawling ice cavern, hoarding every sound that entered the valley. When travelers sang songs of hope, or children shouted in play, Kaelen froze their voices into silent, glittering crystals. He gave nothing back, leaving the mountain passes desolate and stripped of trust.

Angered by this selfish silence, the Sun Weaver decided to end Kaelen’s monopoly. She captured the brightest flame of dawn and forged it into a radiant golden tuning fork. Descending into the freezing, dark cavern, she struck the golden fork against the canyon floor. A note so resonant and warm exploded outward, piercing the frozen stillness.

Unable to withstand the pure harmony of the sunlit note, the ice crystals shattered into thousands of glowing droplets. The ancient earth gods, furious at Kaelen’s greed, enchanted the melting shards. They transformed them into the Echoes, unseen spirits of the cliffs forever stripped of the ability to hoard. Bound by a magical law of reciprocity, the Echoes must faithfully bounce back every call. Now, the canyons always return the voices they are given, ensuring an eternal trust.
